thread:
Connor O'Brien: Locking contents for Console 2025.04 release train by EOD. Need final call on what Route Experiments ships vs gets cut. Please reply w/ “in / out” + any blocking risk.

Connor O'Brien: Current candidate list (high level):
1) Console UI: list/details + creation wizard (flagged)
2) Results dashboard (latency/cost/error deltas + guardrail banners)
3) Console API: create/update/start/stop + audit trail fetch
4) RBAC gates for mutations
5) Audit log events for lifecycle
6) Telemetry: experiment_id/variant_id propagation to OTel + rollups powering results
7) Guardrails: soft-stop + notifications
8) Optional hard-stop on severe p99 regression (kill switch)
9) Backfill tooling for metrics schema changes

Connor O'Brien: Cut line proposal is after (7). (8)-(9) out unless we get strong SRE + data signoff.

Marissa Cole: Product vote: keep creation + basic results + audit/RBAC in. Hard-stop default should not ship in 2025.04; we can mention “coming soon” but not GA promise. Backfill can be behind the scenes, not a release-train deliverable.

Dylan Brooks: +1. Console side: wizard + list/details are stable behind feature flag. Results dashboard is *mostly* stable; biggest risk is query cost + “results not updating” perception if rollups lag.

Felix Schneider: Results view is ready for cut if needed (we can ship list/details + create/start/stop first). But if we ship without results, beta customers will complain. I’d prefer we keep results in but restrict drill-down filters (route/model/region) to reduce heavy queries.

Chloe Martin: Backend APIs (create/update/start/stop, status) are good. Two notes:
- Stop semantics: we have “stopping” -> “stopped” with drain; Console reflects intermediate state now.
- Pagination perf: list-experiments API still needs the index tweak from the thread last week. Not a blocker but I want it in before train cut.

Jada Williams: Policy engine + router integration are in good shape. Precedence rules are implemented as decided: experiment selection happens before fallback policy evaluation. I want to be careful about overlapping experiments on the same route; we block by default in validation (unless you explicitly set priority).

Logan Wright: Telemetry is the biggest release risk. We have experiment attribution in spans + rollups, but we’re still seeing attribution drop on streaming retries in staging sometimes. The fix is in PR-28622; needs to be in the train or we’ll have noisy/misleading results.

Allison Grant: Observability POV: if results ship, we need the standard dashboards + at least the “attribution drop rate” panel and propagation lag metric visible to oncall. Otherwise we’re blind when customers say “variant B is 0 traffic” or “results stale”.

Sean Gallagher: SRE call: ship soft-stop + notification only. Hard-stop is fine *only* if (a) behind kill switch, (b) default off, (c) runbook links wired into alert payloads, and (d) we agree on thresholds & alerting severity. I’d rather defer (8) to 2025.05 if we’re tight.

Rafael Mendes: +1 to Sean. We also need to avoid paging ourselves to death on attribution drop. Alert windows and severities need tuning; current staging signal is noisy.

ReleaseBot: Reminder: Release cut for 2025.04 branch is 2025-03-28 18:00 PT. Feature flags must default OFF in prod unless explicitly approved.

Connor O'Brien: Ok. Proposed “IN” list for 2025.04:
- (1) Console UI list/details + creation wizard (feature-flagged, allowlist)
- (2) Results dashboard w/ reduced drill-down (no route/model/region combinatorial filters at launch)
- (3) Console API create/update/start/stop + status
- (4) RBAC gates for mutations
- (5) Audit log events for lifecycle (+ export fields)
- (6) Telemetry propagation + rollups powering results
- (7) Guardrails soft-stop + notifications
“OUT / DEFER”:
- (8) Optional hard-stop (keep merged if safe but do NOT enable; or cut from train)
- (9) Backfill tooling as formal deliverable (data team can run as needed)

Connor O'Brien: Need explicit yes/no on hard-stop PR inclusion. It can exist behind kill switch but still adds surface area.

Sean Gallagher: Prefer OUT of the release train. If it’s merged, it’s harder to reason about blast radius during rollout. We can re-introduce next train with a game day.

Marissa Cole: OUT. We already aligned with execs that GA scope doesn’t include “stat-sig” and we also shouldn’t expand to automatic rollback beyond soft-stop in this train.

Dylan Brooks: OUT from train. Also, for results dashboard, can we add a banner copy like “Metrics update every ~5–10m” and show last rollup timestamp? That will cut Support tickets.

Felix Schneider: I can add “last updated” + tooltip in results view this week. That’s a small change and helps a ton.

Logan Wright: For attribution correctness, I need PR-28622 (streaming retries) IN. Also PR-28631 (prop lag metric) should be in; otherwise we can’t distinguish rollup lag vs config staleness.

Allison Grant: +1. And we should ship the linkable runbook URL in the alert payloads (even if alerts aren’t on by default for customers). It helps internal oncall.

Rafael Mendes: Fine with dashboards/rules landing; just keep paging thresholds conservative for beta allowlist. We can start with ticket-only notifications in #eng-sre if needed.

Chloe Martin: I’ll land the list API index fix + guard the expensive joins. That should reduce DB spikes when more experiments exist.

Jada Williams: Validation edge cases: if we’re blocking overlapping experiments, Console should show clear error copy. Otherwise people will try and hit a confusing 400. Can we confirm this is in scope?

Marissa Cole: In scope. UX spec has copy for “Route already has an active experiment”. Ship the stricter validation; we can add “priority override” later.

Connor O'Brien: Decision recorded:
- 2025.04 ships Route Experiments beta surface (create/start/stop + results + soft-stop) behind feature flag/allowlist.
- Hard-stop is CUT from 2025.04 train.
- Required for train: streaming attribution fix + propagation lag metric + “last updated” timestamp in results.

Connor O'Brien: Risk assessment (for notes):
1) Data quality: attribution drop on streaming/retries → mitigated by PR-28622 + dashboards.
2) Perceived staleness: rollup/propagation lag → mitigate by “last updated” + prop lag metric + runbook.
3) Cardinality/cost: experiment dimensions → mitigated by restricted tagging + reduced filters in Console.
4) Operational safety: guardrails false positives → soft-stop only; no automatic hard-stop.

Connor O'Brien: I’ll update the release train doc + cutlist. If anything above slips past 03/28, we’ll pull results dashboard first (not creation/start/stop).

Dylan Brooks: :thumbsup: works for me. We’ll keep results behind the same flag so we can disable it independently if queries spike.

Sean Gallagher: :+1: Please add a checklist item: run the propagation lag gameday before expanding allowlist.

Connor O'Brien: Added. Thanks all.
